Alive

A brain that grows its own cells in the cloud, every hour, with its owner's PC off: its arms write candidate cells, a locked judge grades each one on held-out questions, and only the survivors join it.

Cells, one arm per domain

Self-modification

One edit to its own procedure per generation, kept only when the next generation's survival rate (survivors over candidates, every lane) rises above the baseline; else the file is written back.

Cortex

The model whose arms write the cells. The pointer moves to a challenger only when the challenger scores higher on the held-out tasks over the paired arms of one tournament.

Dreams and curriculum

After each generation a proposer arm writes tasks just past what the brain answers, a solver arm answers them, and the ones the brain still misses become its next misses. The curriculum is the seed set a human session wrote, one class per domain.
